name: The Owl That Attended
description: During the monthly overnight fellowship at Bethel Prayer Mountain, a large owl landed on the windowsill at 1:00 AM and remained for forty-seven minutes. Eleven of the twenty-two members present left the building immediately. Four stayed to pray against it specifically. Three attempted to photograph it. The owl departed without incident. Within six weeks, two of those who fled experienced misfortune. The fellowship has held two special sessions to discuss the theological implications. No consensus has been reached.
prose: The monthly overnight prayer fellowship at Bethel Prayer Mountain, Kisii, was in its third hour on the night of 7 February 2014 when, at approximately 1:00 AM, a large owl landed on the outer sill of the east-facing window and settled there with the composure of something that had intended to arrive. The fellowship at the time comprised twenty-two members engaged in intercessory prayer.

The owl's arrival was noted sequentially, beginning with Sister Moraa, seated nearest the east window, whose sharp intake of breath caused the adjacent members to look up, which caused the members beyond them to look up, until all twenty-two were looking at the window. The owl looked back. It was large. Its eyes were described by six separate witnesses as 'yellow,' 'very yellow,' 'too yellow,' 'yellow and knowing,' and, by one witness, simply as 'a problem.'

Eleven members left the building immediately and did not return that night. This group included three deacons, the fellowship treasurer, and the woman who had been leading the prayer at the moment of arrival, who dropped the microphone in a manner that produced significant audio feedback. Four members — led by Brother Elkana Nyamweya — formed a prayer circle and began rebuking the owl directly and at volume, citing Psalms 91 and Luke 10:19. Three members attempted to photograph it using mobile phones. The owl sat for forty-seven minutes, during which Brother Nyamweya's rebuking group increased in intensity without visible effect on the owl. The owl then departed of its own accord.

In the six weeks following the fellowship, two of the eleven who had fled experienced misfortune: one lost a significant business contract and one was involved in a minor road accident from which she recovered fully. The remaining nine who fled, the four who prayed against the owl, and the three who photographed it all experienced no recorded misfortune. The fellowship has convened two special sessions to discuss the theological implications. No consensus has been reached. The incident is OPEN.
heritageTrustNote: Two of the three mobile phone photographs have been lost to phone replacements. The third was recovered and shows a blurred window and what may be a large bird or may be a reflection. It has been catalogued as Exhibit OWL-01. Brother Nyamweya stands by the rebuke. The owl has not returned, as far as can be confirmed.

pullQuote.quote: I was not running. I was relocating my prayer to the outside. There is a difference. Also it was very large.
pullQuote.attribution: Deacon Zablon Omari, 55, One of the eleven who left

objectRecord.currentLocation: Heritage Trust Digital Archive. Catalogued as Exhibit OWL-01.
